 School in Cebu suspends face-to-face classes due to dengue cases
 By Kaiser Jan Fuentes
 November 16, 2026
 80
 Resize 
 Small 
 Medium 
 Large 
 TALISAY CITY, Cebu—A public elementary school here will implement modular distance learning for one week as health officials address a clustering of dengue cases among its students.
 Tabunok Central Elementary School will temporarily suspend face-to-face classes while the City Health Office, Dengue Task Force and school personnel carry out cleaning and mosquito-control activities within the campus.
 Mayor Samsam Gullas announced the preventive measure on Monday following an assessment by the City Health Office.
 “This will give our City Health Office, Dengue Task Force, and school personnel sufficient time to conduct intensive cleaning, inspections, larval control, and removal of possible mosquito breeding sites within the school premises,” Gullas said.
 The local government will reassess the situation after a week.  It may extend the suspension for another week if the clustering continues and if the City Health Office recommends additional precautions.

 Gullas clarified that the suspension applies only to in-person classes, with students continuing their education through alternative learning arrangements.
 “Education is important, but we should never compromise the health and safety of our students and teachers,” he said.
 Advertisement 
 Separately, all public schools in Talisay City will adopt adjusted class schedules to limit exposure to extreme heat, following consultations with the Department of Education (DepEd), school supervisors and school officials.
 The city government cited reports of uncomfortable classroom temperatures due to high student-to-classroom ratios, extreme heat in school premises, increasing cases of nose bleeding among students and elevated blood pressure among teachers.
 Officials also considered the heat exposure of learners while commuting to and from school.
 The adjusted schedules will prioritize earlier and cooler hours, with individual schools determining their specific arrangements based on their capacity and in coordination with DepEd.
 Advertisement 
 Gullas said the citywide adjustment would provide a coordinated response to concerns raised by public schools instead of allowing each institution to address similar conditions independently.
 He also referred to Executive Order 130 issued by President Ferdinand Marcos Jr., which provides for localized class suspensions, including school-level decisions based on conditions affecting the safety of students and school personnel, subject to applicable guidelines.
 The City Health Office and Dengue Task Force, meanwhile, will continue surveillance in other schools in Talisay. 
 The local government has also conducted misting activities in public and private schools, along with inspections and larval control.
 Advertisement 
 Gullas encouraged families, teachers and students to remove stagnant water and keep their surroundings clean to prevent mosquito breeding.
 Private schools and Talisay City College, meanwhile, may determine their own class schedules and learning arrangements through their respective administrations, following applicable guidelines.
 The developments in Talisay add to the measures being prepared by other local government units in Cebu to address extreme heat amid the anticipated Super El Niño.
 In Mandaue City, the DepEd division has adopted the 4H guidelines, which classify heat conditions into Hayo, Hinay, Hinga and Hinto based on school-level heat index readings. 
 Advertisement 
 The classifications guide decisions on regular classes, shortened schedules, home-based learning and class suspensions.
 In Lapu-Lapu City, the local government and DepEd division are developing guidelines for suspending face-to-face classes during extreme heat. 
 The Local School Board discussed the proposed protocols, the 4H guidelines and school risk assessments during its eighth regular meeting on Nov. 9.
 Minglanilla public schools, meanwhile, began implementing four-hour daily classroom sessions on Nov. 16. Morning classes run from 6 a.m. to 10 a.m., while afternoon classes take place from 2 p.m. to 6 p.m.
 Advertisement 
 In Cebu City, the City Council approved a resolution recommending face-to-face classes for elementary pupils from 5:30 a.m. to 10 a.m. from Monday to Thursday, with Modular Distance Learning every Friday. The proposal still needs evaluation by the Cebu City Local School Board. KAISER JAN FUENTES
